_readme: WHAT THE REPO BELIEVES IS DEPLOYED, as a measured fact rather than as prose.
One entry per function whose live body this repo has an opinion about — every
hash-pinned / programmatically-patched body (derived by sweep() in
tests/live-hash-drift.mjs), every body three or more migrations restate, and
the program floor. `live` is what production ACTUALLY had when it was last
computed IN SQL on each side — POSIX class, never '\s+' (the two runtimes
THIS FILE IS THE DEPLOYMENT RECORD. Its diff is how a reviewer sees that a
body on production moved. Regenerate ONLY with --live --write, and only when
the change was intended. Never edit a hash by hand to make a build green —
a red hash is the check working.

functions.name: hr_put_client_state__ungated
functions.why: VERIFIED 2026-08-31 with  node tests/live-hash-drift.mjs --codediff  (strips SQL comments outside string/dollar-quote literals from both bodies and compares): CODE-IDENTICAL, 2,366 code chars — BUT THE CAUSE IS A DEFECT, not documentation. The production body stores its box-drawing comment characters DOUBLE-ENCODED (U+2500 arrived as the CP1252 reading of its UTF-8 bytes), which is the entire 152-char delta. Cosmetic today because it is confined to comments; it proves an apply path mangled UTF-8, and the same path applied to a string literal (an error code, a jsonb key, an item id) would be a silent behaviour change. Measured 2026-08-31: 1 of 264 public functions on production is affected. Flagged live.mojibake:true so a SECOND occurrence goes red. Fix requires re-applying 2026-08-22-client-state-denylist.sql / 2026-08-28-client-state.sql through a UTF-8-clean path — a production DDL write, and therefore NOT taken without explicit authorisation.

functions.sig: hr_record_rejection(p_user uuid, p_slot integer, p_intent text, p_code text, p_detail jsonb, p_count bigint)
functions.name: hr_record_rejection
functions.why: STAGED, NOT APPLIED - and for once the divergence is CODE, not comments, ON PURPOSE. supabase/migrations/2026-09-07-companion-codes-severity.sql (Security ruling C6) is in the apply manifest and therefore in the replay, and it has NOT been applied to production: it patches this body to put 'unknown_unlock' in c_incident and 'missing_req_item' in c_escalating. So the repo rebuilds a body that really is different from the deployed one, and --codediff will correctly report CODE DIFFERS until the Coordinator applies. The live half is UNCHANGED and still the value MEASURED on production 2026-08-31 (md5 48f44dae7cb0503b3003f8740a875f29, normalised length 3051, re-read read-only the same day): c_incident holds its 22 codes and c_escalating holds rate_limited, own_listing, intent_mismatch. It was deliberately NOT pre-updated to a hash that is not live yet. THE PRE-EXISTING, COMMENT-ONLY HALF OF THIS DIVERGENCE STILL STANDS and is why the two shapes have to be handled together: VERIFIED 2026-08-31 with  node tests/live-hash-drift.mjs --codediff  that the bodies were CODE-IDENTICAL at 1,639 code chars, because 2026-08-11-player-state.sql expanded three comment blocks after the apply (why rate_limited is not an incident on its own, the own_listing wash-trading rationale, the severity ratchet note) and corrected a cross-reference from S6c-ii to S6c. Production therefore carries SHORT comment blocks around both classification arrays and the replay carries LONG ones - which is exactly why the C6 migration anchors on PURE CODE lines that are byte-identical in both shapes (measured read-only against production 2026-08-31: each anchor matches exactly once), and why tests/companion-codes-severity.mjs installs the comment-stripped body and applies the migration on top of it. AFTER THE APPLY: run  node tests/live-hash-drift.mjs --live --write  and let the baseline diff be the deploy record. The expected post-apply live hash is the replay hash recorded here only if production's comment blocks were also brought into line; if it is not, re-run --codediff and expect the residual difference to be comments only again.
